title: “見たくても見られない”問題の解消へ　Ｊ１・ファジアーノ岡山本拠地の新スタジアム検討協議会始動「より開かれた議論」目指し実現可能性を探る【岡山発】
extracted_text: サッカーＪ１、ファジアーノ岡山の本拠地となる新スタジアムの検討協議会が４月２６日、岡山県庁で開かれた。今後の議論のポイントを探る。 大学関係者や経済界の代表など１０人で構成されている検討協議会。２６日の会合ではスタジアム建設に詳しい日本女子体育大学の上林功教授が座長に任命された。 「様々な条件を鑑みながら実現可能性を調べる調査だと認識している」と上林教授。建設ありきではなく必要性を問いたいともしていて、やはり建設は難しい、という話があればそういった議論も協議会で行うべきと表明した。 岡山県が運営する「ＪＦＥ晴れの国スタジアム」を巡っては２０２５年、Ｊ１・ファジアーノ岡山の全ての試合でホーム側のチケットが完売し、多くの人が観戦できない状態となった。 サポーターらが新たなスタジアムの整備を求めて約５０万人分の署名を岡山県に提出。協議会はこうした動きを受けて県が設置、スタジアムの適切な「規模」やスポーツ観戦以外にも使えることを想定した「機能』、整備可能な「場所」など具体案を検討していく。 また「コスト」や「経済効果」なども算出し、今後１、２カ月に１回の会合を開いて整備の是非を県に提案します。 上林功教授は１年をめどに提案を行う方向で、「皆さんの意見がスタジアム建設に関わるという自分事にしてもらいたい」と、協議会では意見集約の仕組みを構築することを提案すべきと述べた。 新スタジアムの整備を推進する会の河野良亮さんは「色々な人が協議会の生の映像が見られる環境を作ってほしい。（新スタジアムの）必要性についてしっかりと議論してもらい、その中でどんなスタジアムが良いか話が出てくると思うので、その順番を県は事務局として決めてほしい」と語った。
translated_text: A study council for a new stadium to serve as the home ground of J1 Fujiano Okayama was held on April 26 at the Okayama Prefectural Office, to explore key points for future discussions. The study council consists of 10 members, including university officials and business representatives. At the April 26 meeting, Professor Akira Kamibayashi of Japan Women's College of Physical Education, who is well-versed in stadium construction, was appointed as chair. 'I see this as a survey to investigate feasibility while taking various conditions into account,' Professor Kamibayashi stated. He also expressed a desire to question the necessity rather than assuming construction will happen, saying that if it turns out construction is indeed difficult, such discussions should also take place within the council. Regarding the 'JFE Sunny Country Stadium' operated by Okayama Prefecture, in 2025, home-side tickets for all J1 Fujiano Okayama matches were sold out, leaving many people unable to attend. Supporters submitted approximately 500,000 signatures to Okayama Prefecture requesting the development of a new stadium. In response to these movements, the prefecture established the council, which will examine specific proposals for the appropriate 'scale' of the stadium, 'functionality' that allows use for purposes other than sports viewing, and possible 'locations' for development. Additionally, they will also calculate 'costs' and 'economic effects,' and will hold meetings roughly once every one to two months to propose to the prefecture whether to proceed with development. Professor Akira Kamibayashi aims to deliver a proposal within about one year, stating, 'I want everyone to make the matter of stadium construction their own personal concern,' and suggesting that the council should establish a system for gathering opinions. Mr. Ryotaro Kono of the association promoting the new stadium development said, 'We want the prefecture to create an environment where people can watch live footage of the council meetings. We want thorough discussions about the necessity of a new stadium, and within that, ideas about what kind of stadium would be best will emerge, so we want the prefecture as the secretariat to decide on that order of proceedings.'
title_en: Addressing 'Wanted to See But Couldn't See' Problem - New Stadium Study Council for J1 Fujiano Okayama's Home Ground Launches Aiming for 'More Open Discussions' to Explore Feasibility [From Okayama]
